concepts.def: Forcing molten plastic into a closed mould under pressure, ideal for producing very large numbers of identical, accurate components.
Heating a thermoplastic sheet until soft, then drawing it down over a mould using suction to form thin shell-shaped products.
Computer numerical control machining, in which programmed machine tools cut material precisely and repeatably from digital design data.
Making a single unique product to a client's exact requirements, typically using skilled labour and accepting a high cost per unit.
Making a set quantity of identical products in groups, with the flexibility to switch the same equipment between different batches.
High-volume manufacture of standardised products on production lines, giving a low unit cost once the large set-up investment is recovered.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Final Production — a core area of Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Final Production brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Final Production.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Injection moulding is most appropriate when a product requires:
options: Very large numbers of identical plastic parts
One unique handmade item
Parts carved from solid timber
Components that are all slightly different

mcqs.q: CNC machining is classed as which type of process?
options: Additive
Subtractive - it cuts material away under computer control
Joining
Finishing only

mcqs.q: Vacuum forming requires the material to be:
options: A thermoplastic sheet that softens when heated
A thermosetting resin that has fully cured
A solid metal billet
A liquid poured into a sealed mould

mcqs.q: A bakery making 200 loaves of one bread type, then switching the same equipment to make 150 rolls, is using:
options: Continuous production
One-off production
Batch production
Mass production

mcqs.q: What is the difference between vacuum forming and injection moulding?
options: Vacuum forming is used for metals and injection moulding for wood.
They are interchangeable names for the same plastic process.
Vacuum forming shapes a heated thermoplastic sheet over a mould using suction; injection moulding injects molten plastic into a closed mould under high pressure.
Yes - because mass-produced goods are always higher quality.

mcqs.q: Is mass production the best choice for every product?
options: Yes - mass production always gives the lowest total cost.
No - mass production only pays off at high volumes; for small quantities or custom products, the enormous tooling and set-up costs make batch or one-off production more economical.
Vacuum forming is used for metals and injection moulding for wood.
Yes - because mass-produced goods are always higher quality.

mcqs.q: Are CNC machining and 3D printing the same thing?
options: Yes - both are computer controlled, so they are the same process.
Yes - CNC is simply the older name for 3D printing.
No - CNC machining is subtractive, cutting material away from a block, while 3D printing is additive, building the part up layer by layer.
Yes - because mass-produced goods are always higher quality.
